entry.title: On the Security of MPC-in-the-Head Signatures with Correlated GGM Trees
entry.summary:
Recent MPC-in-the-Head techniques enable the construction of signature schemes with compact signature sizes from various hardness assumptions. These techniques rely on commitments based on GGM trees, which have been optimized to further reduce the signature size with the so-called one-tree or correlated tree optimizations. While the one-tree technique has no incidence on the security of the scheme, this is not obvious for the correlated tree technique, and a formal security analysis of this technique has been missing in the literature.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Phoenix: Hash-and-Sign with Aborts from Lattice Gadgets
entry.summary:
Preimage sampling is a fundamental tool in lattice-based cryptography, and its performance directly impacts that of the cryptographic mechanisms relying on it. In 2012, Micciancio and Peikert proposed a new way of generating trapdoors (and an associated preimage sampling procedure) with very interesting features. Unfortunately, in some applications such as digital signatures, the performance may not be as competitive as other approaches like Fiat-Shamir with Aborts.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: Aker: Efficient Two-Party SLH-DSA
entry.summary:
Threshold signing is widely deployed to protect cryptographic keys, but extending these deployments to post-quantum signatures remains challenging. While NIST's lattice-based signatures now have efficient threshold protocols, distributed signing for SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), NIST's stateless hash-based signature standard, has been considered prohibitively expensive because it lacks the algebraic structure those protocols typically exploit. We present Aker, a maliciously secure two-party signing protocol compatible with an unmodified FIPS 205 verifier.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems #post-quantum
